data.body:
PHASE 2 COMPLETE — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1401
(https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1401), commit 209778de4e.

TEST (RED -> GREEN, held out from the fix subagent).
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py`
- `test_the_guard_scans_the_modules_that_hold_the_calls` — the non-vacuity/coverage
  assertion. Computes, independently of the guard, which DC modules actually contain a
  `search_issues` call, and requires the guard's scan population to cover them.
  Legitimately RED first: "AssertionError: the pagination guard never scans
  ['_base.py', '_issues.py']".
- `test_the_guard_would_catch_an_uncapped_call_in_a_non_transport_module` — teeth driven
  through the REAL sources (strips every explicit cap in-memory, requires an offender from
  a non-transport module). Legitimately RED first: "stripping every explicit cap from the
  DC adapter sources produced NO offenders".
Both were physically removed from the working tree while the fix subagent worked, and
re-applied only for validation. MUTATION CHECK: re-pinning `_guard_scanned_sources()` to
`{"transport.py": ...}` (the exact confirmed root cause) returns both to RED; restoring the
fix returns them to GREEN. The tests have teeth.

FIX. `_guard_scanned_sources()` now globs every `*.py` in the DC adapter package instead of
reading `transport.py` alone, and `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default(sources)` takes
its source population as an argument, reporting offenders as `<module>.py:<line>` so a
failure names the file. No `src/` file changed; no pagination behaviour touched.

REPLICATION OF THE ORIGINAL REPORT. The ticket's stated symptom was that the guard "would
not notice a fifth unpaginated caller added anywhere in the DC adapter". Appending a real
uncapped `self._client.search_issues(f"project = {k}")` to `_links.py` now fails the guard
with "['_links.py:115']". Before the fix, that same addition was invisible.

GATES. `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` 2266 passed; the module itself 23 passed
(21 -> 23, no test removed); `make lint` and `make typecheck` (mypy, 432 files) clean.

FIX-SAFETY AUDIT. Restoration, not creation — the guard's scope is restored to the
population it had before 465d's split, no new capability. No new dependency (`re` is
stdlib). No test weakened: no assertion removed, no skip/xfail added; the single expectation
change is `["line 3"]` -> `["synthetic.py:3"]`, a literal-for-literal update that ADDS file
attribution.

SIBLINGS (Step 7).
- Axis 1, construct sweep: a full audit of `tests/` for single-target structural guards
  found FOUR more confirmed-vacuous by the same mechanism —
  `apply/test_applier_repair_property.py:24,136` (scans `applier.py`, now a re-export
  facade; the policed function moved to `apply_inbound.py`),
  `test_llm_timeouts.py:335-336` (scans `llm/runner.py`; timeout code moved to
  `structured_run.py`/`agent_call.py`),
  `fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py:62` (scans `inbound_probe.py`, now a 55-line
  vocabulary module; mechanics in `adapters/jira/probe.py`), and
  `test_usage_log_pricing_qualified_2ca9.py:118` (scans `llm/usage_log.py`, which contains
  zero string-parsing calls at all). Plus two borderline (`test_bedrock_provider.py:119`,
  `test_code_review_assemble.py:88-92` — the latter also uses a cwd-relative path) and two
  at-risk hardcoded scan lists (`test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py:511-514`,
  `test_container_roster.py:103-118`) that already leak instances outside their scan set.
  Filed as bug 8a5e-b88e-0c3e-4544, linked `discovered_from` this ticket, rather than
  fixed here: each re-target is its own reviewable unit and can surface unrelated offenders.
- Axis 2, parity sweep: the rule is "a whole-project paged read must not take the
  `search_issues`/page default". The parallel surface is the CLOUD adapter's equivalent
  guard, `test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py` — NOT missing: it already carries
  `test_the_structural_guard_actually_sees_the_three_known_readers` (line 630), the exact
  anti-vacuity assertion this ticket adds, and globs `adapters/jira/*.py` rather than one
  file. Its own comment at ~626 even notes "DC's equivalent guard scans only the DC
  transport" — the vacuity was foreseen on the Cloud side and is now closed on the DC side.
  No MISSING slot.

RESIDUAL RISK & PREVENTION. The audit's one generalizable finding: every structural guard
that SURVIVED a module relocation has an explicit anti-vacuity assertion
(`test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py:630`, `test_web_tool_gating.py:130`); none of the
vacuous ones did. Disposition: ticket filed (8a5e), whose acceptance criteria require that
pattern on each repaired guard. A repo-wide lint for "structural guard without a coverage
assertion" would be the structural prevention, but that is a design decision, not this
bug's repair — noted on 8a5e rather than built here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: all three met (guard scans the package; a teeth test proves the
widened predicate reports a non-transport offender; the other-guards audit is reported
above and ticketed as 8a5e).
